items.stem: 按照国际货币基金组织的汇率制度分类，以下属于软钉住汇率制度的是（ ）。
items.explanation: 按照国际货币基金组织（IMF）的汇率制度分类，属于软钉住汇率制度的是 ：（1）传统钉住，该制度要求一国货币与另一国或一篮子货币保持固定兑换比率货币当局可采用直接干预手段维持固定汇率。相比于硬钉住制度，传统钉住制度并不要求该国对汇率不变做出任何承诺，因此货币政策存在一定的灵活性。（2）稳定化安排，该制度要求一国与一国或一篮子货币的即期汇率波幅控制在2%以内并维持半年及以上。（3）爬行钉住，平时汇率固定不变，但视通货膨胀的程度，每隔一段时间作微小的调整。（4）准爬行盯住，汇率相对固定，但有某种程度的管理或干预。（5）水平区间盯住，类似于传统盯住，但波动幅度大于±1％。故选BCD项。

items.section: 四、英语阅读理解题
items.stem: According to the passage, the price system is related primarily to ______.
items.explanation: 细节理解题。本题考查对文章关键信息的理解和提取能力，重点关注价格体系相关联的主要元素。文章第一段明确指出 “The price system of the United States is a very complex network composed of the prices of all the products bought and sold in the economy as well as those of a myriad of services, including labor, professional transportation, and public -utility services”，表明价格体系主要与产品和服务相关。A选项中的劳动只是服务的一部分；B选项中的交通和保险，保险在文中未提及；C选项中的公用事业只是服务的一种，且维修未提及。所以答案选D，产品和服务是价格体系主要关联的对象。
items.passage:
短文（一）Price determine how resources are to be used. They are also the means by which products and services that are in limited supply are rationed among buyers. The price system of the United States is a very complex network composed of the prices of all the products bought and sold in the economy as well as those of a myriad of services, including labor, professional transportation, and public-utility services. The interrelationships of all these prices make up the“system”of prices.
The prices of any particular product or service are linked to a broad, complicated system of prices in which everything seems to depend more or less upon everything else.
If one were to ask a group of random individuals to define“price”, many would reply that price is an amount of money paid by the buyer to the seller of a product or service or, in other words, that price is the money value of a product or service as agreed upon in a market transaction. This deﬁnition is, of course, valid as far as it goes.
For a complete understanding of a price in any particular transaction, much more than the amount of money involved must be known. Both the buyer and the seller should be familiar with not only the money amount, but with the amount and quality of the product or service to be exchanged, the time and place at which the exchange will take place and payment will be made,the form of money to be used, and the credit terms and discounts that supply to the transaction,guarantees on the product or service, delivery terms, return privileges, and other factors. In other words, both buyer and seller should be fully aware of all the factors that comprise the total“package”being exchanged for the asked-for amount of money in order that they may evaluate a given price.

items.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT a factor in the complete understanding of price?

options.A: Instructions that come with a product.

items.explanation: 细节理解题。本题考查对文章中关于理解价格所涉及因素的全面理解，判断选项是否在文章提及范围内。文章第三段提到 “Both the buyer and the seller should be familiar with not only the money amount, but with the amount and quality of the product or service to be exchanged, the time and place at which the exchange will take place and payment will be made, the form of money to be used, and the credit terms and discounts that supply to the transaction, guarantees on the product or service, delivery terms, return privileges, and other factors”。B选项产品的数量、C选项产品的质量、D选项产品的保修（对应guarantees on the product or service）均有提及，而A选项产品附带的说明书在文中未出现，所以答案是A。

items.section: 四、英语阅读理解题
items.stem: In the last sentence of the passage, the word“they”refers to ______.
items.explanation: 语义理解题。本题考查对文中代词指代对象的判断能力，依据上下文逻辑关系来确定。文章最后一句“In other words, both buyer and seller should be fully aware of all the factors that comprise the total“package”being exchanged for the asked - for amount of money in order that they may evaluate a given price”，根据前文提到买卖双方需要了解各种因素，这里“they”是为了评估价格，所以“they”指代的是买卖双方，即C选项。按照寻找代词指代对象的方法，先向上搜索最近的名词，这里最近的就是“both buyer and seller”，代入句子后语义通顺，可确定答案。A项的政府与消费者保护协会、B项的经济学家与金融分析师和D项的监管者与行业专家都在该句中未涉及，不选，因此答案是C。

items.section: 四、英语阅读理解题
items.stem: The paragraph following the passage most likely discusses ______.

options.B: types of payment plans for service
options.C: theories about how products aﬀect diﬀerent levels of society
options.D: how certain elements of price“package”inﬂuence its market value

items.explanation: 文章后续内容推断题。本题考查对文章整体逻辑和后续内容走向的推断能力，依据文章结尾内容进行合理推测。文章最后一段强调买卖双方要了解构成价格“package”的所有因素才能评估价格，接下来最有可能讨论的是这些价格“package”的某些元素如何影响其市场价值，即D选项。A选项不寻常的产品广告方式、B选项服务的支付计划类型、C选项产品如何影响社会不同层面，在文章中均未提及相关线索，与文章结尾内容逻辑不符。一般来说，推断下文题重点关注尾句，尾句提出了价格 “package” 的概念，所以下文围绕其相关内容展开讨论，因此答案是D。

items.section: 四、英语阅读理解题
items.stem: What is the best title for the passage?

options.A: The Inherent Weakness for the Price System
options.B: The Complexities of the Price System
options.D: Resource Allocation and the Public Sector

items.explanation: 主旨大意题。本题考查对文章主旨的把握和概括能力，用简洁准确的标题来涵盖文章核心内容。文章主要介绍了美国价格体系的复杂性，包括其构成以及理解价格所需要考虑的诸多因素。A选项价格体系的内在弱点在文中未提及；C选项交易中的信用条款只是理解价格的一个因素，不能概括全文；D选项资源分配和公共部门偏离了文章主要讨论的价格体系内容。B选项 “The Complexities of the Price System”（价格体系的复杂性）准确地概括了文章主旨，所以答案选B。一般拟定标题可以从文章的主要内容、核心观点出发，简洁明了地体现文章主题，这个标题包含了文章重点讨论的对象 “价格体系” 以及其主要特点“复杂性”，因此答案是B。106. 【答案】D细节理解与推断题。本题考查对段落细节信息的理解与推断能力。选项A错误，原文第一段明确提到“即将成为濒危物种”（about to turn cash into an endangered species），而非已经成为。选项B错误，第二段提到政府可以通过数字化“更严密监控欺诈或逃税”（keep closer tabs on fraud），但并未说明能彻底解决（tackle）。选项C错误，第一段指出过去十年数字支付 “迅速发展”（taken oﬀ），与“rarely seen”矛盾。选项D正确，第二段首句明确提到数字支付使经济更高效（make the economy more eﬃcient），因此答案是D。

items.section: 四、英语阅读理解题
items.stem: What can we learn from the ﬁrst two paragraphs?

options.A: Cash has already become an endangered species in rich economies.
options.B: Governments can tackle the problem of fraud by digitalization.
options.C: Digital payments are rarely seen in recent years.
options.D: Electronic payments will bring more eﬃciency to the economy.

items.explanation: 原文在前一题解析末尾写有‘106.【答案】D’，并指出数字支付使经济更高效。
items.passage:
短文（二）For the past 3,000 years, when people thought of money they thought of cash. From buying food to settling bar tabs, day-to-day dealings involved creased paper or clinking bits of metal.Over the past decade, however, digital payments have taken oﬀ. Now this revolution is about to turn cash into an endangered species in some rich economies. That will make the economy more eﬃcient—but it also poses new problems that could hold the transition hostage.
In the main the prospect of a cashless economy is excellent news. When payments dematerialize, people and shops are less vulnerable to theft. Governments can keep closer tabs on fraud or tax evasion. Digitalization vastly expands the playground of small businesses and sole traders by enabling them to sell beyond their borders. It also creates a credit history, helping consumers borrow.
Yet set against these beneﬁts are a bundle of worries. Electronic payment systems may be vulnerable to technical failures, power blackouts and cyber-attacks — this week Capital One, an American bank, became the latest ﬁrm to be hacked. In a cashless economy the poor, the elderly and country folk may be left behind. And eradicating cash, an anonymous payment method, for a digital system could let governments snoop on people’s shopping habits and private titans exploit their personal data.
These problems have remedies. First, governments need to ensure that central banks’monopoly over coins and notes is not replaced by private monopolies over digital money. Rather than letting a few credit-card firms have a stranglechold on the electronic pipes for digital payments, governments must ensure the payments plumbing is open to a range of digital ﬁrms which can build services on top of it. They should urge banks to oﬀer cheap, instant, bank-to-bank digital transfers between deposit accounts.
Second, governments should maintain banks’ obligation to keep customer information
private, so that the plumbing remains anonymous. Digital ﬁrms that use this plumbing to oﬀer services should be free to monetize transaction data, through, for example, advertising, so long as their business model is made explicit to users. Some customers will favor free services that track their purchases; others will want to pay to be left alone.
Last, the phase-out of cash should be gradual. For a period of ten years, banks should be obliged to accept and distribute cash in populated areas. This will buy governments time to help the poor open bank accounts, educate the elderly and beef up internet access in rural areas. The rush towards digital money is the result of spontaneous demand and innovation. To pocket all the rewards, governments need to prepare for the day when crumpled bank notes change hands for the last time.
items.correctionNote: 答案被误排在前一题解析末尾，按题号106关联。

items.stem: Capital One is mentioned in Paragraph 3 to illustrate ______.

options.A: digital payment systems are susceptible to network attacks
options.B: American banks will become easier to hack
options.C: a digital system could let private giants steal people’s data
options.D: country people will be aﬀected in a cashless world

items.explanation: 细节理解与推断题。本题考查例证与论点的逻辑关系，识别作者意图。第三段主旨句为第二句”Electronic payment systems may be vulnerable to technical failures, power blackouts and cyber-attacks —this week Capital One... became the latest ﬁrm to be hacked.”电子支付系统可能面临技术故障、停电和网络攻击，Capital One被黑客攻击是对这一风险的具体例证，其中选项A正确，直接对应“vulnerable to cyber-attacks”。选项B过度推断，案例仅说明某银行被攻击，未提及“美国银行更容易被黑”。文章并没有直接将Capital One的黑客事件与私人公司窃取用户数据的风险相联系，因此选项C不符合文意。文章没有讨论无现金社会的影响，因此选项D也不符合。因此答案是A。
items.passage:
短文（二）For the past 3,000 years, when people thought of money they thought of cash. From buying food to settling bar tabs, day-to-day dealings involved creased paper or clinking bits of metal.Over the past decade, however, digital payments have taken oﬀ. Now this revolution is about to turn cash into an endangered species in some rich economies. That will make the economy more eﬃcient—but it also poses new problems that could hold the transition hostage.
In the main the prospect of a cashless economy is excellent news. When payments dematerialize, people and shops are less vulnerable to theft. Governments can keep closer tabs on fraud or tax evasion. Digitalization vastly expands the playground of small businesses and sole traders by enabling them to sell beyond their borders. It also creates a credit history, helping consumers borrow.
Yet set against these beneﬁts are a bundle of worries. Electronic payment systems may be vulnerable to technical failures, power blackouts and cyber-attacks — this week Capital One, an American bank, became the latest ﬁrm to be hacked. In a cashless economy the poor, the elderly and country folk may be left behind. And eradicating cash, an anonymous payment method, for a digital system could let governments snoop on people’s shopping habits and private titans exploit their personal data.
These problems have remedies. First, governments need to ensure that central banks’monopoly over coins and notes is not replaced by private monopolies over digital money. Rather than letting a few credit-card firms have a stranglechold on the electronic pipes for digital payments, governments must ensure the payments plumbing is open to a range of digital ﬁrms which can build services on top of it. They should urge banks to oﬀer cheap, instant, bank-to-bank digital transfers between deposit accounts.
Second, governments should maintain banks’ obligation to keep customer information
private, so that the plumbing remains anonymous. Digital ﬁrms that use this plumbing to oﬀer services should be free to monetize transaction data, through, for example, advertising, so long as their business model is made explicit to users. Some customers will favor free services that track their purchases; others will want to pay to be left alone.
Last, the phase-out of cash should be gradual. For a period of ten years, banks should be obliged to accept and distribute cash in populated areas. This will buy governments time to help the poor open bank accounts, educate the elderly and beef up internet access in rural areas. The rush towards digital money is the result of spontaneous demand and innovation. To pocket all the rewards, governments need to prepare for the day when crumpled bank notes change hands for the last time.

items.section: 四、英语阅读理解题
items.stem: According to Paragraph 4, governments ought to ______.

options.A: let credit-card ﬁrms control the electronic pipes
options.B: ensure that central banks’ monopoly over digital money
options.C: urge banks to oﬀer cheap, instant, bank-to-bank digital transfers
options.D: make sure the payments plumbing is open to all digital ﬁrms

items.explanation: 细节理解题。本题考查对具体建议的细节理解，精准定位到文章第四段的内容。选项A错误，原文Let credit-card ﬁrms control the electronic pipes明确反对信用卡公司垄断（not replaced by private monopolies）。原文Ensure that central banks’monopoly over digital money虽然原文提到中央银行应保持对货币的控制，但并没有明确表示要确保中央银行对数字货币的垄断，因此选项B不完全准确。选项C正确，对应“urge banks to oﬀer cheap,instant, bank-to-bank digital transfers”。选项D错误，原文为“open to a range of digitalﬁrms”（对多家公司开放），而非“all”（所有公司）。因此答案是C。

items.section: 四、英语阅读理解题
items.stem: Banks need to accept and distribute cash in populated areas because ______.

options.A: cash should be quickly phased out
options.B: it will give governments time to help the poor
options.C: it is the result of spontaneous demand

items.explanation: 细节理解题。本题考查因果关系的逻辑推理，需结合上下文。原文第5段In the meantime, banks need to accept and distribute cash in more populated areas, allowing governments time to ﬁgure out how to help people who would be aﬀected by a cashless society.可知银行需要在拥挤地区接受并分发现金，以便政府有时间帮助那些可能受到无现金社会影响的群体。选项B正确，直接对应“buy governments time to help the poor”。选项A与“gradual phase-out”矛盾。原文主要谈论的是为了解决贫困问题而采取的措施。没有证据表明银行接受和分发现金是自发需求的结果，因此C不对。原文并没有提到现金的分发会直接促进数字创新，重点是帮助政府应对无现金社会的挑战，因此D不对。因此答案是B。

items.source: 真题/2025年财经岗-金管局笔试真题及解析.md
items.section: 四、英语阅读理解题
items.stem: Which of the following can best summarize the main idea of the text?

options.A: How to phase out cash and to build up a cashless world.
options.B: The pros and cons of digital payment and how to tackle its problems.
options.C: The indispensable role of governments and banks in digital payment.
options.D: The possibility of the private monopolies over digital money.

items.explanation: 主旨大意题。本题考查对文章整体结构和核心论点的把握。文章结构为：优势（第二段）→ 问题（第三段）→ 解决方案（第四至六段）。选项B正确，涵盖“利弊分析”和“解决措施”。文章没有仅仅讨论淘汰现金，而是更多关注如何应对无现金社会带来的挑战，因此选项A不全面。尽管文章确实提到政府和银行的作用，但它更侧重于讨论数字支付的优缺点和解决方案，而非单纯强调它们的不可或缺性，因此选项C不全面。虽然文章提到私营公司可能垄断数字支付，但文章的重点是讨论数字支付的问题和如何应对，而不是垄断本身，因此选项D不全面。因此答案是B。

items.source: 真题/2025年财经岗-金管局笔试真题及解析.md
items.section: 四、英语阅读理解题
items.stem: Why are many people opposed to monitoring employee performance?

options.A: It puts workers under constant pressure.
options.B: It is universally deemed anti-human by nature.
options.C: It does both mental and physical harm to employees monitored.
options.D: It enables ﬁrms to squeeze maximal productivity from employees.

items.explanation: 细节理解题。本题考查反对监控的核心原因。由题干中的opposed以及monitoring employee performance定位到第一段第一句。文章第一段第一句提到许多人反对工作场所监控，因为这种做法本身就带有使人丧失人性的效果，同时，还会带来无尽的压力。文中的relentless pressure对应A项中的constant pressure，故选A项。选项B错误，原文为 “inherent dechumanizing”，但未提及“universally anti-human”。选项C错误，文中未提 “身心伤害”。选项D是监控的目的，而非反对原因。因此答案是A。
items.passage:
短文（三）Many oppose workplace surveillance, because of the inherent dechumanizing eﬀect it has and the relentless pressure it brings. But it’s on the rise around the world as ﬁrms look to become more eﬃcient by squeezing more productivity from their workers. More than half of companies with over $750 million in annual revenue used“non-traditional”monitoring techniques on staﬀlast year.
Monitoring employee performance gives firms the ability to assess how their staff are performing and interacting, which can be good for both the firm and employees themselves.A growing number of analytics companies offer this service. They gather“data exhaust”left by employees’ email and instant messaging apps, and use name badges equipped with radio-frequency identiﬁcation devices and microphones. These can check how much time you spend talking, your volume and tone of voice, even if you do not dominate conversations. While this may sound intrusive, exponents argue that it can also protect employees against bullying and sexual harassment.
Some of this data analysis can produce unexpected results. For example, it was found that people who sat at 12-person lunch tables tended to interact, share ideas more and outperform those who regularly sat at four-person tables, a fact that would probably have gone undetected without such data analysis.
Over the last few years a Stockholm co-working space called Epicenter has gone much further and holds popular“chipping parties”, where people can have microchips implanted in their hands. They can use the implants to access electronically-controlled doors, or monitor how typing speed correlates with heart rate. Implanted chips may seem extreme, but it is a relatively small step from ID cards and biometrics to such devices.
As long as such schemes are voluntary, there will probably be a growing number of convenience-oriented uses so that a substantial number of workers would opt to have a chip inserted. But if implanted chips are used to reduce slack time or rest breaks, that could prove
to be detrimental. And if surveillance tools take away autonomy, that’s when they prove most unpopular. A lot depends on how such monitoring initiatives are communicated and this could prevent possible revolts being staged.
If bosses don’t communicate eﬀectively, employees assume the worst. But if they’re open about the information they’re collecting and what they’re doing with it, research suggests 46% of employees are generally okay with it. Although many such monitoring schemes use anonymised data and participation is voluntary, many staﬀers remain skeptical and fear an erosion of their civil liberties.
So workplace surveillance could be empowering for staﬀ and useful for companies looking to become more eﬃcient and proﬁtable. But implemented in the wrong way, it could also become an unpopular tool of oppression that proves counterproductive.

items.source: 真题/2025年财经岗-金管局笔试真题及解析.md
items.section: 四、英语阅读理解题
items.stem: What is the supporters’ argument for workplace surveillance?

options.A: It enables employees to refrain from dominating conversations.
options.B: It enhances employees’ identiﬁcation with ﬁrms they work in.
options.C: It can alert employees to intrusion into their privacy.
options.D: It can protect employees against aggressive behavior.

items.explanation: 细节理解题。本题考查支持者的观点。由题干中的supporters' argument定位到第二段最后一句。文中第二段最后一句提到支持者认为这可以保护员工免受欺凌和性骚扰protect against bullying and sexual harassment，欺凌和性骚扰都是侵犯性的行为，因此工作场所监控可以保护员工免受攻击性行为的侵害，选项D正确，对应“aggressive behavior”。选项A是监控手段（检测对话主导权），非论点。选项B和C原文未提及。因此答案是D。

items.section: 四、英语阅读理解题
items.stem: What does the author want to show by the example of different numbers of people interacting at lunch tables?

options.A: Data analysis is key to the successful implementation of workplace surveillance.
options.B: Analyzing data gathered from workers can yield something unexpected.
options.C: More workmates sitting at a lunch table tend to facilitate interaction and idea sharing.
options.D: It is hard to decide on how many people to sit at a lunch table without data analysis.

items.explanation: 细节理解和推断题。本题为例证作用题，考查案例与论点的关系。由题干中的diﬀerent numbers of people interacting at lunch tables定位到第三段首句和第二句。文章第三段第二句举了一个例子：人们发现，与经常坐在四人桌旁的人相比，坐在12人用餐桌旁的人更愿意互动、分享更多的想法，并且表现得更好。文中的例子都是为了支持某个论点服务的，也就是为本段第一句服务的。第一句提到某些数据分析可能会产生意想不到的结果，因此，不同数量的人在午餐桌上互动的例子是为了证明分析从员工那儿收集到的数据可以得到让人意想不到的结果produce unexpected results，故选B项。选项C是案例内容，非论证目的。选项A和D过度引申。因此答案是B。

items.section: 四、英语阅读理解题
items.stem: What does much of the positive eﬀect of monitoring initiatives depend on?

options.A: How frequently employees are to be monitored.
options.B: What speciﬁc personal information is being excluded.
options.C: What steps are taken to minimize their detrimental impact.
options.D: How well bosses make known their purpose of monitoring.

items.explanation: 细节理解题。本题考查影响监控效果的核心变量。由题干中的monitoring initiatives定位到第五段最后一句。文中第五段最后一句指出，监控举措要想有积极效果，很大程度上取决于如何传达此类监控措施。第六段第一、二句提到，如果老板不能与员工进行有效沟通，员工会把事情想得很糟糕。但是，如果他们对正在收集的信息以及对这些信息的处理持开放态度，研究表明，46%的员工通常都是能接受的。原文强调“沟通方式”（how initiatives are communicated）决定效果。选项A（频率）、B（排除信息）、C（减少负面影响）均未提及。因此答案是D。

Some of this data analysis can produce unexpected results. For example, it was found that people who sat at 12-person lunch tables tended to interact, share ideas more and outperform those who regularly sat at four-person tables, a fact that would probably have gone undetected without such data analysis.
Over the last few years a Stockholm co-working space called Epicenter has gone much further and holds popular“chipping parties”, where people can have microchips implanted in their hands. They can use the implants to access electronically-controlled doors, or monitor how typing speed correlates with heart rate. Implanted chips may seem extreme, but it is a relatively small step from ID cards and biometrics to such devices.
As long as such schemes are voluntary, there will probably be a growing number of convenience-oriented uses so that a substantial number of workers would opt to have a chip inserted. But if implanted chips are used to reduce slack time or rest breaks, that could prove
to be detrimental. And if surveillance tools take away autonomy, that’s when they prove most unpopular. A lot depends on how such monitoring initiatives are communicated and this could prevent possible revolts being staged.
If bosses don’t communicate eﬀectively, employees assume the worst. But if they’re open about the information they’re collecting and what they’re doing with it, research suggests 46% of employees are generally okay with it. Although many such monitoring schemes use anonymised data and participation is voluntary, many staﬀers remain skeptical and fear an erosion of their civil liberties.
So workplace surveillance could be empowering for staﬀ and useful for companies looking to become more eﬃcient and proﬁtable. But implemented in the wrong way, it could also become an unpopular tool of oppression that proves counterproductive.

items.section: 四、英语阅读理解题
items.stem: What concern do monitoring initiatives cause among many staﬀers?

options.B: They may erode the workplace environment.
options.C: They may infringe upon staﬀers' entitled freedom.
options.D: They may become counterproductive in the long run.

items.explanation: 细节理解与推断题。本题考查员工的主要顾虑。由题干中的staﬀers定位到第六段最后一句。第六段最后一句提到尽管许多此类监控计划使用匿名数据，而且是自愿参与的，许多员工仍然持怀疑态度，担心他们的公民自由会受到侵害，由此可见员工担忧监控举措会侵犯他们应有的自由，文中的liberties对应C项中的freedom，故选C项。选项D是实施不当的后果，非员工直接担忧。选项A和B原文未提及。因此答案是C。116. 【答案】A细节理解题。本题考查对人物观点的精准定位。A建议对AI进行社会控制，B否认AI进步的紧迫性，C赞扬AI科学的巨大成功，D因潜在风险而对AI评价低。第一段明确提到Russell认为AI科学需要“social limitations”，第二段进一步主张建立 “system of checks” 和法规（“regulations”）来处理系统性偏见。所以A选项正确，他建议社会控制。选项B（否认AI进步的紧迫性）错误。Russell仅强调AI进步需要时间，但未否认其紧迫性（第一段提到“doesn't make it science ﬁction”）。选项C（赞扬AI科学的成功）错误。原文未提及对AI成功的赞扬，反而指出其风险未被合理评估。选项D（因潜在风险而对AI评价低）不准确。Russell并非否定AI本身，而是强调需通过社会控制管理风险。因此答案是A。

items.section: 四、英语阅读理解题
items.stem: According to Paragraph 1 and Paragraph 2, Stuart Russell ______.

options.B: denied the imminence of AI progress
options.C: praised AI science for its great success
options.D: had a low opinion of AI for its potential risks

items.explanation: 原文在前一题解析末尾写有‘116.【答案】A’，说明 Stuart Russell 主张为 AI 建立社会约束与检查机制。
items.passage:
短文（四）“Progress in AI is something that will take a while to happen, but that doesn’t make it science fiction,”said Stuart Russell, the University of California computing professor, and co-author of the top AI textbook. The science of AI is a human enterprise that requires social limitations. The risks, however are not being properly weighed. There are two emerging approaches to AI. The ﬁrst is to view it engineering terms, where algorithms（算法）are trained on speciﬁc tasks. The second presents deep philosophical questions about the nature of human knowledge.
The former is very much pushed by Silicon Valley, where AI is deployed to get products quickly to market and problems dealt with later. This has led to AI“succeeding”even when the goals aren't socially acceptable and they are pursued with little accountability. The pitfalls of this approach are highlighted by the role YouTube's algorithm plays in radicalizing people, given that there is no public understanding of how it works. Prof. Russell argues, reasonably, for a system of checks where machines can pause and“ask”for human guidance, and for regulations to deal with systemic biases.
The academic also backs global adoption of EU legislation that would ban impersonation of humans by machines. Computers are getting closer to passing, in a superﬁcial way, the Turing test — where machines attempt to trick people into believing they are communicating with other humans. Yet human knowledge is collective: to truly fool humans a computer would have to be able to grasp mutual understandings. OpenAI’s GPT-3, probably the best non-human writer ever, cannot comprehend what it spews. When Oxford scientists put it—and similar AIs—to the test this year, they found the machines produced false answers to questions that “mimic popular misconceptions and have the potential to deceive”. It so troubled one of OpenAI’s own researchers that no one knew how such language is being made that he left to set up an AI safety
lab.
Some argue that AI can already produce new insights that humans have missed. But human intelligence is much more than an algorithm. Inspiration strikes when a brilliant thought arises that can’t be explained as a logical consequence of preceding steps. Einstein’s theory of general relativity cannot be derived from observations of that age—it was experimentally proven only decades later. Human beings can also learn a new task by being shown how to do it only a few times. Machines, so far, cannot. Currently, AI can be prompted—but not prompt itself—into action.
Humans are stumbling into an era when the more powerful the AI system, the harder it is to explain its actions. How can we tell if a machine is acting on our behalf and not acting contrary to our interests? Such questions ought to give us all pause for thought.
items.correctionNote: 答案被误排在前一题解析末尾，按题号116关联。

items.section: 四、英语阅读理解题
items.stem: The approach of viewing AI in engineering terms has ______.

options.A: questioned the nature of human knowledge
options.D: sped up the market entry of quality products

items.explanation: 细节理解题。本题考查因果关系与细节匹配。选项B（导致社会责任缺失的算法）正确。第二段指出硅谷推动的工程方法导致AI在目标不被社会接受时仍被推进，且缺乏问责（如YouTube算法引发激进化）。选项A（质疑人类知识的本质）错误。这属于第二种方法（哲学方法）的特点，与工程方法无关。选项C（防止算法激进化）错误。原文明确提到工程方法导致了算法激进化（“highlighted by the role YouTube's algorithm plays in radicalizing people”）。选项D（加速优质产品上市）错误。原文仅提到“quickly to market”，未提及“quality products”。因此答案是B。

items.section: 四、英语阅读理解题
items.stem: According to Prof. Russell, machines ______.

options.A: should be banned from pretending to be humans
options.B: are especially helpful to counter social biases
options.C: might get uniformly regulated at a global scale
options.D: are not supposed to be supervised by humans

items.explanation: 细节理解题。本题考查人物观点与具体建议。选项A（应禁止冒充人类）正确。第三段明确提到Russell支持欧盟立法禁止机器冒充人类（“ban impersonation of humans by machines”）。选项B（特别有助于消除社会偏见）错误。原文仅提到法规需处理系统性偏见，未说明机器本身的作用。选项C（可能在全球范围内统一监管）不准确。Russell支持“global adoption of EU legislation”，但未提及“uniformly regulated”。选项D（不应由人类监督）错误。Russell主张机器需“ask for human guidance”，说明需要人类监督。因此答案是A。

items.section: 四、英语阅读理解题
items.stem: What does the author say about OpenAI’s GPT-3?

options.A: Its language is impossible to understand.
options.B: It is non-human but can truly fool humans.
options.C: Its programming is based on misconceptions.
options.D: It is intelligent but cannot comprehend words.

items.explanation: 细节理解题。本题考查具体信息的同义替换。选项D（智能但无法理解语言）正确。第三段指出GPT-3“cannot comprehend what it spews”，且测试中生成错误答案，模仿误解。选项A（其语言无法理解）错误。原文强调GPT-3自身无法理解生成内容，而非人类无法理解其语言。选项B（能真正愚弄人类）错误。原文提到GPT-3只是“superﬁcially”接近图灵测试，实际无法理解“mutual understandings”。选项C（编程基于误解）错误。GPT-3生成的内容模仿误解，但编程基础并非基于误解。因此答案是D。

items.section: 四、英语阅读理解题
items.stem: Einstein’s theory of general relativity is mentioned to show that ______.

options.A: AI-produced insights can be complementary to human thoughts
options.B: machines are comparable to humans in terms of logical thinking
options.C: human intelligence can hardly be translated into an algorithm
options.D: brilliant scientiﬁc ideas always come way ahead of their time

items.explanation: 细节理解题。本题考查例子与论点的关系。选项C（人类智能难以转化为算法）正确。最后一段用爱因斯坦的理论说明人类智能能产生无法通过逻辑推导的灵感，而AI依赖算法，无法做到这一点。选项A（AI见解可补充人类思想）错误。例子强调人类智能的独特性，而非AI的补充作用。选项B（机器在逻辑思维上与人类相当）错误。例子反驳了这一观点，强调人类智能的不可替代性。选项D（科学思想常超前于时代）偏离主题。例子重点在于人类智能的非算法性，而非时间先后。因此答案是C。

items.stem: 实际 GDP 等于（）。

options.A: 价格水平除以名义 GDP
options.B: 名义 GDP 除以价格水平
options.C: 名义 GDP 乘以价格水平

items.explanation: 实际 GDP=名义 GDP/GDP 平减指数，GDP 平减指数表示价格水平。故选 B 项。

items.explanation: 根据总供给—总需求模型，当总供给曲线向右上方倾斜时，扩张性的财政政策使得总需求曲线右移，产出增加，物价水平上升；当总供给曲线垂直于横轴时，扩张性的财政政策使得总需求曲线右移，但不会增加产出，只会提高物价水平。故选 D 项。

items.stem: 当达到市场均衡时，买者是支付愿望 ___ 的人，卖者是成本 ___ 的人。
items.explanation: 在经济学中，把潜在买方对某种商品的支付意愿定义为他愿意为之支付的最高价格。消费者剩余就是消费者愿意支付的最高价格与实际支付价格之差。把某个潜在卖方愿意接受的最低价格称为卖方成本。生产者剩余就是生产者愿意出卖的最低价格与实际成交的价格之差。市场均衡时，消费者剩余与生产者剩余都达到最大。故选 B 项。

options.C: 与可支配收入无关的消费总量
options.D: 与可支配收入相关的消费总量

items.explanation: 消费函数是反映消费支出与影响消费支出的因素之间的函数关系式。消费函数可以表示为 $C=\alpha+\beta Y$。式中，$\alpha$ 为自发消费部分，$\beta$ 为边际消费倾向，$\beta$ 和 Y 的乘积表示收入引致的消费。因此，消费函数的斜率取决于边际消费倾向 $\beta$。故选 A 项。

items.explanation: 外汇交易基本类型包括：（1）即期外汇交易（现汇交易），是外汇市场上最常见、最普遍的外汇交易形式；（2）远期外汇交易（期汇交易），是指交易双方在成交后并不立即办理交割，而是按照事先约定的币种、金额、汇率、交割时间、地点等交易条件，到约定时期才进行实际交割的外汇交易；（3）掉期交易，是指将币种相同、金额相同但方向相反、交割期限不同的两笔或两笔以上的交易结合在一起进行的外汇交易，这种交易形式常用于银行间外汇市场上。故选 C 项。

items.stem: 根据托宾 q 理论，货币政策将通过下列哪项的影响而作用于实际的经济活动，从而达到预期的最终目标？
items.explanation: 根据托宾 q 理论，货币政策通过对股票价格的影响而作用于实际的经济活动，从而达到预期的最终目标。托宾的 Q 比率是公司市场价值对其资产重置成本的比率。当 Q>1 时，购买新生产的资本产品更有利，这会增加投资的需求；当 Q<1 时，购买现成的资本产品比新生产的资本产品更便宜，这样就会减少资本需求。故选 D 项。

items.stem: 关于基准利率，下列说法错误的是（）。

options.A: 基准利率是起决定作用的利率
options.B: 基准利率是无风险利率
options.D: 基准利率必须是市场化利率

items.explanation: 基准利率是多种利率并存下起决定性作用的利率；在市场经济中，基准利率是指通过市场机制形成的无风险利率，是一种市场化的利率。国债利率只是基准利率的一种，不能直接认定基准利率就是国债利率。故选 C 项。

items.stem: 经济资本是商业银行在一定的置信水平下，为应对未来一定时期内资产的（）而持有的资本，其规模取决于自身的（）和风险管理策略。

options.A: 预期损失、实际风险水平
options.B: 非预期损失、实际风险水平
options.C: 灾难性损失、预期风险水平
options.D: 非预期损失、预期风险水平

items.explanation: 经济资本是指商业银行在一定的置信水平下，为了应对未来一定期限内资产的非预期损失而应该持有的资本金。根据经济资本的定义，经济资本是一种取决于商业银行实际风险水平的资本，商业银行的整体风险水平高，要求的经济资本就多，反之则要求的经济资本就少。故选 B 项。

options.A: 不运用或不直接运用银行的自有资金
options.B: 不承担或不直接承担市场风险
options.C: 以收取服务费（手续费、管理费）赚取价差的方式获得收益

items.explanation: 商业银行中间业务是指不构成商业银行表内资产、表内负债，形成银行非利息收入的业务，商业银行以代理人的身份为客户办理的各种业务，目的是为了获取手续费收入。商业银行参与的信用活动是资产负债表内的业务。故选 D 项。

items.stem: 李先生以自己为被保险人投保了一份保额 40 万元的终身寿险。投保时，李先生将自己的实际年龄 40 岁虚报为 38 岁，而该保险产品在李先生投保时 40 岁对应的保费为 800 元，38 岁对应的保费为 760 元。若干年后李先生死亡，保险公司发现李先生虚报了年龄。李先生指定的受益人可以获得的保险金是（）。

items.stem: 以下关于凯恩斯货币理论的描述，正确的是（）。

options.A: 货币在长期和短期来看都是中性的
options.B: 货币在长期来看是中性的
options.C: 货币在短期来看是非中性的，具有实际效应

items.explanation: 凯恩斯主义认为，货币不受经济运行影响，但货币供应量的变化能够影响经济运行，因此凯恩斯理论认为货币是非中性的，长期和短期都是非中性的。故选 CD 项。

items.stem: 正是由于长期生产的（）的作用，决定了 LAC 曲线表现出先下降后上升的 U 形特征。
items.explanation: 长期成本曲线呈 U 型，主要是由长期生产中的规模经济和规模不经济决定的。在企业生产扩张的开始阶段，厂商由于扩大生产规模而使经济效益提高，叫做规模经济；当企业生产扩张到一定规模后，厂商继续扩大生产规模，就会使经济效益下降，叫做规模不经济。短期平均成本曲线呈 U 型，是因为边际报酬递减规律的作用。故选 AB 项。

items.stem: 金融监管是首先从银行监管开始的，这和商业银行的一些特性有关，包括（）。

options.A: 银行具有信用创造功能
options.B: 银行具有资金中介功能
options.C: 银行具有期限转换功能
options.D: 银行具有票据清算功能

items.explanation: 金融监管首先是从对银行进行监管开始的。这和银行的一些特性有关，包括：（1）银行提供的期限转换功能，即银行在储蓄到投资的转化过程中，为储蓄者提供短期资产和流动性，把储蓄集合起来，再根据投资者的需要提供期限相对较长的负债和资金，从而实现期限转换；（2）银行是整个支付体系的重要组成部分，作为票据的清算者，降低了交易的费用；（3）银行的信用创造和流动性创造功能。这三大特性使得维持银行业的稳定性成为必要。故选 ACD 项。

items.stem: According to this passage, insurance is possible because ___ .

options.A: only a small proportion of the insured suffer loss
options.B: everyone at some time suffers loss

items.explanation:
细节理解题。本题的问题是“根据文意，保险是可行的，原因是 ___ ”。A项，“被保险人中只有一小部分真正蒙受损失”；B项，“所有人都有蒙受损失的时候”；C项，“几乎所有人都蒙受损失”；D项，“只有被保险人蒙受损失”。根据题目中关键词找到主题句：On the other hand, not every house is damaged by fire nor every vessel lost at sea. 解释了不是所有人都会遭受损失，只有一小部分人会遭到厄运，因此保险是切实可行的。故选A项。
细节理解题。本题的问题是 “第一自然段中，短语 the pool of contribution（款项总额）的意思是 ___ 。” A 项，“保险公司支付的款项”；B 项，“管理保险的费用”；C 项，“被保险人支付的款项”；D 项，“每笔保险费的金额”。根据题目中关键词找到主题句：If these persons each put a small sum of money into a pool, there will be enough to meet the needs of the few who do suffer loss. In other words, the losses of the few are met from the contributions of the money. This is the basis of insurance. 短语 “the pool of contribution” 是使用了修辞手法，其实质就是保险费的总和，即被保险人支付的款项。故选 C 项。
细节理解题。本题的问题是“对普通商业风险进行投保是不可行的，原因是 ___ ”。A项，“此类风险所需费用昂贵”；B项，“此类风险不能被准确预估”；C项，“此类风险发生率太高”；D项，“保险费用太高”。根据题目中关键词找到主题句：Not all risks can be covered by insurance. Broadly speaking, the ordinary risks of business and speculation cannot be covered. 主题句中，解释了不能对普通商业风险进行投保的原因是无法预估此类风险，只有在风险可以预估的情况下才能对风险投保。故选B项。
细节推理题。本题的问题是“保险单上有时使用过时词语，原因是 ___ ”。A项，“法庭决定不使用时髦词语”；B项，“它被所有的被保险人广泛接受”；C项，“它使普通人能够轻松理解”；D项，“此类词语的含义已被确定”。根据题目中关键词找到主题句：The wording of policies, particularly in marine insurance, often seems very old-fashioned, but there is a sound reason of this. Over a large number of years, many law cases have been brought to clear up the meanings of doubtful phrases in policies. 主题句中，使用过时词语的原因是此类词语含义清晰，不会引起矛盾。故选D项。
观点态度题。该题询问作者对保险的态度。A项，把保险看作一种赌博，文章并未提及此事，排除；B项，是一种赚快钱的方式，保险并没有此种功能，文章也未提及，排除；C项，有用且必要的，从作者对保险业务的成型到保单的签订，都做了很详细的说明，可以推断作者认为保险是有用的，符合题意；D项，说保险是过时的，是文章中形容一些保单措辞的表达，和保险业无关，排除。根据题目中关键词找到主题句：Insurance is the sharing of risks. Nearly everyone is exposed to risk of some sort. 主题句中，作者明确表示几乎所有人都有可能遭受风险，而保险能够分担风险，因此保险是有用而且必需的。故选 C 项。
细节理解题。本题的问题是“从第一段中，我们能得知反向抵押贷款 ___ ？”A项，“反向抵押贷款本来的预期是帮助老年人留在家里”；B项，“反向抵
押贷款正在将所有的老年人赶出家门”；C项，“反向抵押贷款只欢迎老年人”；D项，“任何老年人都能申请反向抵押贷款”。根据题目中关键词找到主题句：The very loans that are supposed to help seniors stay in their homes are in many cases pushing them out. Reverse mortgages, which allow homeowners 62 or older to borrow money against the value of their homes and not pay it back until they move out or die, have long been said with problems. 可以看出反向抵押贷款的初衷本来是帮助老年人留在家中，但往往结果是使老年人丧失房产。B项“all”，C项“only”，D项“any”，说法都过于绝对。故选A项。
细节理解题。本题的问题是“关于反向抵押贷款的问题正确的说法是？”A项，一些贷款机构不愿意把钱借给老年人，与文章第二段第一句话 Some lenders are aggressively recommending loans to seniors who cannot afford the fees associated with them, without mentioning the property taxes and maintenance. 不符，排除；B项，“借款人无法如预期中归还款项”；C项，“联邦和州监管部门正在制定反对意见”；D项，“一些放款人破产了”。根据题目中关键词发现，本题与第一题主题句相同，可以看出反向抵押贷款的最大问题是借款方老年人无法按时还款，因此可能损失自己的房产。故选B项。
items.passage:
Insurance is the sharing of risks. Nearly everyone is exposed to risk of some sort. The house owner, for example, knows that his property can be damaged by fire, the ship owner knows that his vessel may be lost at sea; the breadwinner knows that he may die at an early age and leave his family the poorer. On the other hand, not every house is damaged by fire nor every vessel lost at sea. If these persons each put a small sum of money into a pool, there will be enough to meet the needs of the few who do suffer loss. In other words, the losses of the few are met from the contributions of the money. This is the basis of insurance. Those who pay the contribution are known as “insured” and those who administer the pool of contributions as “insurers”.
Not all risks can be covered by insurance. Broadly speaking, the ordinary risks of business and speculation cannot be covered. The risk that buyers will not buy goods at the prices offered is not of a kind that can be statistically estimated, and risks can only be insured against if they can be so estimated.
The legal basis of all insurance is the “policy”. This is a printed form of contract. It states that in return for the regular payment by the insured of a certain sum of money, called the “premium”, which is usually paid every year, the insurer will pay a sum of money or compensation for loss, if the risk actually happens. The wording of policies, particularly in marine insurance, often seems very old-fashioned, but there is a sound reason of this. Over a large number of years, many law cases have been brought to clear up the meanings of doubtful phrases in policies. The law courts have given these phrases a definite and indisputable meaning, and to avoid future disputes the phrases have continued to be used in polices even when they have passed out of normal use in speech.

items.stem: What can we learn about mortgage loans from the first paragraph?

options.A: The loans are expected to help seniors stay in their homes.
options.B: The loans are driving all seniors out of their homes.
options.C: The reverse mortgage only welcomes seniors.
options.D: Any senior can apply for reverse mortgages.

items.explanation: 阅读材料第一段介绍反向抵押贷款旨在帮助老年人留在自己的住房中。
items.passage:
The very loans that are supposed to help seniors stay in their homes are in many cases pushing them out. Reverse mortgages, which allow homeowners 62 or older to borrow money against the value of their homes and not pay it back until they move out or die, have long been said with problems. Now, federal and state regulators are documenting new instances of abuse as smaller mortgage brokers, including former sub-prime lenders, flood the market after the recent exit of big banks and as defaults on the loans hit record highs.
Some lenders are aggressively recommending loans to seniors who cannot afford the fees associated with them, without mentioning the property taxes and maintenance. Others are wooing seniors with promises that the loans are free money that can be used to finance their long-desired things, without clearly explaining the risks. Some widows were pressured not to have their names on the contract, without being told that they could be left facing foreclosure after their husbands died.
Now, as the vast baby boomer generation is entering retirement and more seniors struggle with declining savings, the newly established Consumer Financial Protection Bureau is working on new rules that could mean better disclosure for consumers and stricter supervision of lenders. More than 775,000 of such loans are outstanding, according to the federal government.
Concerns about the multi-billion dollar reverse mortgages market echo those raised in the lead-up to the financial crisis when consumers were marketed loans—often carrying hidden risks—that they could not afford. “There are many of the same red flags, including explosive growth and the fact that these loans are often advertised aggressively without regarded to suitability,” sad Lori Swanson, the Minnesota attorney general, who is working on reforming the reverse mortgage market.

items.stem: The phrase “facing foreclosure” most probably implies ___ .

options.A: the widows are pressured to lose their own names
options.B: the widows may be forced to leave their homes
options.C: the widows have misunderstood the reverse mortgage
options.D: the widows do not know what their long-desired things are

items.explanation:
语义题。本题的问题是 “短语‘facing foreclosure’(面临丧失抵押品赎回权) 最可能暗示 ___ ”。定位文章可知，该短语出现在文章第二段最后一句话：Some widows were pressured not to have their names on the contract, without being told that they could be left facing foreclosure after their husbands died. A 项，“寡妇被强迫舍弃自己本来的名字”；B 项，“寡妇可能被强迫离开自己的家”；C 项，“寡妇误解了反向抵押贷款”；D 项，“寡妇不知道自己长久以来渴望得到的东西是什么”。根据本题主题句可知，在签署反向抵押贷款合同时，一些寡妇没有在合同上签字，因此在丈夫去世后，她们可能会丧失自己的房产。故选 B 项。

The very loans that are supposed to help seniors stay in their homes are in many cases pushing them out. Reverse mortgages, which allow homeowners 62 or older to borrow money against the value of their homes and not pay it back until they move out or die, have long been said with problems. Now, federal and state regulators are documenting new instances of abuse as smaller mortgage brokers, including former sub-prime lenders, flood the market after the recent exit of big banks and as defaults on the loans hit record highs.
Some lenders are aggressively recommending loans to seniors who cannot afford the fees associated with them, without mentioning the property taxes and maintenance. Others are wooing seniors with promises that the loans are free money that can be used to finance their long-desired things, without clearly explaining the risks. Some widows were pressured not to have their names on the contract, without being told that they could be left facing foreclosure after their husbands died.
Now, as the vast baby boomer generation is entering retirement and more seniors struggle with declining savings, the newly established Consumer Financial Protection Bureau is working on new rules that could mean better disclosure for consumers and stricter supervision of lenders. More than 775,000 of such loans are outstanding, according to the federal government.
Concerns about the multi-billion dollar reverse mortgages market echo those raised in the lead-up to the financial crisis when consumers were marketed loans—often carrying hidden risks—that they could not afford. “There are many of the same red flags, including explosive growth and the fact that these loans are often advertised aggressively without regarded to suitability,” sad Lori Swanson, the Minnesota attorney general, who is working on reforming the reverse mortgage market.

items.stem: In the restaurant story, the author may most probably think the waiter or waitress was ___ .

items.passage:
Imagine you went to a restaurant with your girlfriend, had a burger, paid with a credit card, and left. The next time you go there, the waiter or waitress, armed with your profile data, greets you with, "Hey Joe, how are you? Mary is over there in the seat you sat last time. Would you like to join her for dinner again?" Then you find out that your burger has been cooked and placed on the table. Forget the fact that you are with another date and are on a diet that doesn't include burgers.
Sound a little bizarre? To some, this is the restaurant equivalent of the Internet. The Net's ability to profile you through your visits to and interactions at websites provides marketers with an enormous amount of data on you—some of which you may not want them to have.
Are you aware that almost every time you access a website you get a “cookie”? Unfortunately, it’s not the Mrs. Field’s recipe. A cookie on the Internet is a computer code sent by the site to your computer—usually without your knowledge. During the entire period of time that you are at the site, the cookie is collecting information about yourself, including where you visit, how long you stay there, and how frequently you return to certain pages.
While this may sound scary enough, cookies aren’t even the latest in technology. A new
system called I-librarian Alexa—named after the legendary third century B.C. library in Alexandria, Egypt—does even more. While cookies track what you are doing at one site. Alexa collects data on all your web activities, such as which site you visit next, how long you stay there, whether you click on advertisements, etc. All this information is available to marketers, who use it to market more effectively to you. Not only do you not get paid for providing the information, you probably don’t even know that you are giving it.

items.source: 真题/【2019】银保监会财经岗·专业卷（附解析）.md
items.stem: According to the first two paragraphs, what will banks in Europe be forced to do?

options.B: To close down the poor services.
options.C: To give up their data monopoly.
options.D: To disclose their sources of profits.

items.explanation: 细节推断题。本题的问题是“根据前两段，欧洲银行被迫做什么？”。从第一段第二句：Banks enjoy a monopoly over data that has helped them get away with poor services and fend off competitors. 可知，银行对数据享有垄断地位，第二段第一句 The rules will compel banks to share data easily with licensed third parties. 说银行不得不与第三方共享数据，可见，银行放弃了他们在数据上的垄断。A 项，“保持客户数据安全”；B 项，“关闭劣质服务”；C 项，“放弃他们的数据垄断”；D 项，“披露他们的利润来源。”故选 C 项。
items.passage:
The data a bank has stored on its servers is more valuable than the gold in its vaults. Banks enjoy a monopoly over data that has helped them get away with poor services and fend off competitors. In Europe, at least, that is all about to change with a new set of regulations, named PSD2.
The rules will compel banks to share data easily with licensed third parties. Bankers in
Europe complain that their profits and customer relationships are under threat. However, opening up banks, and the data they store, is good for consumers and competition. New providers will be better placed to offer all sorts of innovative services, such as a one-click option to put unspent monthly income into a pension plan.
Nevertheless, some concerns about PSD2 are legitimate. In particular, it is reasonable to wonder about the privacy and security implications of sensitive financial data being shared with third parties. But banks themselves are hardly invulnerable to cyber attacks (网络攻击). And the solutions that the European regulators propose to deal with these worries look promising. Third parties that want to use bank data will need to convince national regulators that their data defenses are solid and are subject to annual regulatory inspections.
The gap between writing rules and implementing them is always large. First, consent from customers to provide access to their bank data must be gained explicitly, and the purposes of the data use should be clearly explained. Second, regulators must be very tough both in ensuring that banks open up their infrastructure and in withdrawing the licenses of third parties that break the rules. Third, regulators must also be flexible enough to allow for changes as the market evolves. Since the new entrants will not be licensed to engage in riskier financial activities—such as lending money—it makes sense to regulate them with a lighter touch. But if some Fintech providers do end up becoming systemically important, higher standards of oversight might be necessary.

Third parties that want to use bank data will need to convince national regulators that their data defenses are solid and are subject to annual regulatory inspections.
The gap between writing rules and implementing them is always large. First, consent from customers to provide access to their bank data must be gained explicitly, and the purposes of the data use should be clearly explained. Second, regulators must be very tough both in ensuring that banks open up their infrastructure and in withdrawing the licenses of third parties that break the rules. Third, regulators must also be flexible enough to allow for changes as the market evolves. Since the new entrants will not be licensed to engage in riskier financial activities—such as lending money—it makes sense to regulate them with a lighter touch. But if some Fintech providers do end up becoming systemically important, higher standards of oversight might be necessary.

items.stem: According to paragraph 3, what is the probable reason that privacy concerns about PSD2 are unnecessary?

options.A: Third parties will have to buy fraud insurance.
options.B: Regulators have come up with promising solutions.
options.C: Banks’ defense against cyber attacks is strong.

items.explanation: 细节推断题。本题的问题是“根据第三段，PSD2的隐私问题没有必要担心的可能原因是什么？”。从第三段第三句可知：And the solutions that the European regulators propose to deal with these worries look promising. 欧洲监管机构提出的解决这些担忧的方案看起来很有希望。A项，“第三方将不得不购买欺诈保险”；B项，“监管机构提出了有希望的解决方案”；C项，“银行对网络攻击的防御很强”；D项，“第三方每月检查客户数据。”故选B项。
items.passage:

The rules will compel banks to share data easily with licensed third parties. Bankers in
Europe complain that their profits and customer relationships are under threat. However, opening up banks, and the data they store, is good for consumers and competition. In particular, it is reasonable to wonder about the privacy and security implications of sensitive financial data being shared with third parties. Third, regulators must also be flexible enough to allow for changes as the market evolves. But if some Fintech providers do end up becoming systemically important, higher standards of oversight might be necessary.

items.stem: Which of the following is true in order to successfully implement PSD2?

options.A: Customers are forced to share their bank data.
options.B: Banks are required to open up their entire operational system.
options.C: Regulators should be both tough and flexible.
options.D: Banks and third parties should be regulated with a light touch.

items.explanation:
细节推断题。本题的问题是“为了成功实施 PSD2，以下哪一项是正确的？”。A 项，“客户被迫分享他们的银行数据”；B 项，“银行被要求开放整个操作系统”；C 项，“监管机构应该既强硬又灵活”；D 项，“银行和第三方应该受到轻微管制。”根据原文最后一段第三句和第四句：“Second, regulator must be very tough both in ensuring that banks open up their infrastructure and in withdrawing the licenses of third parties that break the rules. Third, regulators must also be flexible enough to allow for changes as the market evolves.”可知，监管机构需要既强硬又灵活。故选 C 项。
主旨大意题。本题的问题是“这篇文章的主要内容是什么？”A项，“欧洲监管机构面临的挑战”；B项，“欧洲的一项新规则，让银行走向竞争”；C项，“欧洲有缺陷的银行体系的解决方案”；D项，“客户私人银行数据迫在眉睫的威胁。”根据主题句 The rules will compel banks to share data easily with licensed third parties. Bankers in Europe complain that their profits and customer relationships are under threat. 可知，本文主要讲的是欧洲开放银行竞争新规则。故选 B 项。

items.stem: 党的十九大报告指出，我国经济已由（）阶段转向（）阶段，正处于转变发展方式、优化经济结构、转换增长动力的攻关期，建设现代化经济体系是跨越关口的迫切要求和我国发展的战略目标。

options.A: 高速增长 高水平发展
options.B: 高速发展 高水平发展
options.C: 高速增长 高质量发展
options.D: 高速发展 高质量发展

items.explanation: 党的十九大报告指出，我国经济已由高速增长阶段转向高质量发展阶段，正处在转变发展方式、优化经济结构、转换增长动力的攻关期，建设现代化经济体系是跨越关口的迫切要求和我国发展的战略目标。故选 C 项。

items.stem: 供给学派提出的供给管理政策的思想核心是( )。
items.explanation: 供给学派着重分析税制对生产要素供给和利用的效果，他们指出，经济主体从事经营活动所关心的并不是获得的报酬或利润总额，而是减去各种纳税后的报酬或利润净额。在累进税制条件下，边际税率是关键因素，因为经济主体是否多做工作，或增加储蓄和投资，要看按边际税率纳税后增加的净报酬是否合算。供给学派经济政策的核心是减税。故选 B 项。

items.stem: 货币主义认为，菲利普斯曲线所表示的失业与通货膨胀之间的交替关系（）。
items.explanation: 短期菲利普斯曲线表明高通货膨胀率与高失业率不会同时发生，通货膨胀率与失业率是此消彼长的。长期菲利普斯曲线是一条位于“自然失业率”的垂直线，表明失业率与通货膨胀率之间不存在替代关系。故选 B 项。

items.stem: 当总效用增加时，边际效用应该（）。

options.D: 为正值，可能增加也可能减少

items.explanation: 根据边际效用递减规律，在一定时间内，在其他商品的消费数量保持不变的条件下，随着消费者对某种商品消费量的增加，消费者从该商品连续增加的每一消费单位中所得到的效用增量即边际效用是递减的。但只要边际效用大于零，总效用就是增加的。故选 B 项。

items.stem: 如果消费者对于确定性收入的偏好小于有风险条件下期望收入的偏好，那么该消费者属于风险（）。
items.explanation: 如果消费者对于确定性收入的偏好大于有风险条件下期望收入的偏好，那么该消费者是风险回避者；如果消费者对于确定性收入的偏好小于有风险条件下期望收入的偏好，那么该消费者是风险爱好者；如果消费者对于确定性收入的偏好等于有风险条件下期望收入的偏好，那么该消费者是风险中立者。故选 B 项。

items.stem: 一个商品价格下降对其互补品最直接的影响是（）。

options.A: 互补品的需求曲线向右移动
options.B: 互补品的需求曲线向左移动

items.explanation: 商品价格下降会导致该商品的需求量增加，从而其互补品的需求也会增加，在图形上表现为互补品需求曲线向右移动。故选 A 项。

items.stem: 20 世纪 90 年代以来，（ ___ ）替代了资产负债率，成为金融监管指标，这有利于增强金融机构的抗风险能力。
items.explanation: 资本充足率是一家银行的资本总额与其风险加权资产的比率，它是保证银行等金融机构正常运营和发展所必需的资本比率。20世纪90年代以来，资本充足率替代了资产负债率，成为金融监管的主要指标，目的是监测银行抵御风险的能力。故选B项。

items.stem: 应对通货膨胀的对策中，通过公开市场业务出售政府债券属于（）。
items.explanation: 通过公开市场业务出售政府债券收紧市场中的货币供给量，减少经济体系中的货币存量，控制社会总需求，能有效抑制通货膨胀。故选 A 项。

items.stem: 全能银行制在以（）为代表的欧洲大陆国家广为流行。
items.explanation: 全能银行（Universal Banking）源于德国，本是德国银行业的分类概念，但在现代金融里其含义已经超出了统计概念的范畴。全能银行是一种银行类型，它不仅经营银行业务，还经营证券、保险、金融衍生业务以及其他新兴金融业务，有的还能持有非金融企业的股权。故选 C 项。

items.explanation: 并表监管是指监管当局以整个银行集团为对象，对银行集团的总体经营和所有风险进行监督。并表监管是相对于单一机构的监管而言，适用于银行集团以及金融集团的监管。故选 B 项。

items.explanation: 资本监管是审慎银行监管的核心。建立在审慎贷款风险分类、充足计提各类资产损失准备基础上计算的资本充足率，是衡量银行综合经营实力和抵御风险能力的重要指标。故选 B 项。

items.explanation: 金融深化一个最基本的衡量指标是货币化程度，即国民生产总值中货币交易总值所占的比例。货币化程度越低，表明 “自然经济” 和 “物物交换总值” 的比重越高。故选 B 项。

items.stem: 下列债券中，不属于外国债券的是（）。
items.explanation: 外国债券是指外国借款人（政府、私人公司或国际金融机构）所在国与发行市场所在国具有不同的国籍并以发行市场所在国的货币为面值货币发行的债券。典型的外国债券包括扬基债券、武士债券、猛犬债券和熊猫债券等。金边债券是指政府债券。故选C项。

items.stem: A 公司是一家玩具生产企业，为防范生产的玩具给客户造成人身伤害或财产损失等风险，A 公司可以投保（）。
items.explanation:
产品责任保险是指以产品制造者、销售者、维修者等的产品责任为承保风险的一种责任保险，而产品责任又以各国的产品责任法律制度为基础。题中 A 公司以公司生产的产品的责任来投保，防范玩具给客户带来人身伤害或财产损失，符合产品责任保险的范畴。
公众责任保险又称普通责任保险或综合责任保险，它以被保险人的公众责任为承保对象，是责任保险中独立的、适用范围最为广泛的保险类别。所谓公众责任，是指致害人在公众活动场所的过错行为致使他人的人身或财产遭受损害，依法应由致害人承担的对受害人的经济赔偿责任。
雇主责任保险是指被保险人所雇用的员工在受雇过程中从事与保险单所载明的与被保险人业务有关的工作而遭受意外或患与业务有关的国家规定的职业性疾病，所致伤、残或死亡，被保险人根据《中华人民共和国劳动法》及劳动合同应承担的医药费用及经济赔偿责任，包括应支出的诉讼费用，由保险人在规定的赔偿限额内负责赔偿的一种保险。
职业责任保险亦称“职业赔偿保险”，承保专业技术人员因职业上的疏忽或过失致使合同对方或其他人遭受人身伤害或财产损失，依法应承担的赔偿责任。其承保对象，包括医生、会计师、建筑师、工程师、律师、保险经纪人、交易所经纪人与其他专业技术人员；一般由承保对象从事专业技术服务的单位投保。
故选 A 项。

items.stem: 随着生活水平的提高，医疗费用支出不断增长，人们的健康意识也不断提高，越来越多的人加入跑步、健走、游泳等健身锻炼的队伍。从风险管理角度看，这些行为属于( )。
items.explanation: 健身锻炼旨在降低疾病发生的概率，属于损失控制中的损失预防。它没有放弃相关风险活动或消除患病可能性，因此不属于风险回避。保险千题千练第106行同题亦建议选A。关于回避与降低风险的区别，可参见：https://www.nhc.gov.cn/bgt/c100023/201703/a398478d7ebf4ac5af488b4f88e2f980.shtml
items.correctionNote: 同题答案冲突：依据损失预防与风险回避的区别，将B改为A；保留修订依据，不冒称官方答案。

items.stem: 挤出效应发生于( )。

options.A: 货币供给减少使利率提高，挤出了对利率敏感的私人部门支出
options.B: 私人部门增税，减少了私人部门的可支配收入和支出
options.C: 政府支出增加，提高了利率，挤出了对利率敏感的私人部门支出
options.D: 政府支出减少，引起消费支出下降

items.explanation: 挤出效应是指政府支出增加，从而导致市场利率上升，私人投资和支出相应地下降。故选 C 项。

options.A: 预期的未来收入小于现期收入，或利率下降
options.B: 预期的未来收入小于现期收入，或利率上升

options.B: 最低平均成本点的轨迹
options.C: 最低边际成本点的轨迹

items.explanation: 长期总成本曲线是一条从原点出发，随着产量增加而增加的曲线，是无数条短期总成本曲线的包络线，表示长期内厂商在每一产量水平上由最优生产规模所带来的最小生产总成本。故选 A 项。

items.stem: 卡特尔通过（）决定其联合利润最大化的产量水平。

options.A: 使每个厂商的边际成本等于边际收益
options.B: 使卡特尔的边际成本等于市场需求
options.C: 使每个厂商达到供求平衡
options.D: 使卡特尔的边际成本等于边际收益

items.explanation: 卡特尔的产量和价格水平的决定和完全垄断厂商的产量和价格水平的决定是一样的，卡特尔制定统一价格的原则是使整个卡特尔组织的利润最大化，因此必须使卡特尔的边际成本等于边际收益。故选 D 项。

options.B: 会有明显波动而且具有逆周期性
options.D: 不是常数但是可以预测

items.explanation: 凯恩斯流动性偏好理论认为利率是顺周期的：在经济周期扩张阶段，利率和货币流通速度会上升；在经济周期紧缩阶段，利率和货币流通速度会下跌。因此，货币流通速度会有明显波动而且具有顺周期性。故选 A 项。

options.A: 经济资本就是账面资本
options.B: 会计资本是监管部门规定的商业银行应持有的同其所承担的业务总体风险水平相匹配的资本

items.stem: 2018 年，某银行发现客户经理王某本人的存款账户与客户有大额资金往来，考虑到王某平时业绩突出，该银行行长仅对王某进行诫勉谈话。3 个月后，王某失踪，多人上访反映被王某诈骗资金 2000 万元。这个案例中出现问题的内部控制环节是（）。
items.explanation: 内部控制环节中的监督与纠正是指商业银行应建立并保持书面程序，对违规、险情、事故的发现、报告、处置和纠正及预防措施做出规定。在该例子中，银行行长没有正确处置违规现象，没有及时制定纠正与预防措施，导致违规事故的再次发生。故选 C 项。

options.A: 1982 年，墨西哥和巴西政府宣布对西方债权国家延期偿还债务
options.C: 1984 年，大陆伊利诺伊信托银行破产

options.A: 百富勤公司因为一家印尼公司无法按约偿付贷款而遭受 2.35 亿美元的巨大损失
options.B: 20 世纪 70 年代，美国金融市场的收益率曲线向上倾斜，储蓄信贷协会通过吸收短期存款后发放长期固定利率抵押贷款就可以获得稳定收益，但到了 80 年代，收益率曲线发生了逆转，储蓄信贷协会因此陷入困境
options.C: 英国雷克航空公司的收入主要来自英国游客，它用美元融资购置了几架飞机，但后来美元开始坚挺，雷克航空公司因入不敷出而破产
options.D: 1995 年，具有 233 年悠久历史的巴林银行破产，破产的直接原因是一位 28 岁的交易员在衍生品交易中造成巨额损失

items.explanation: 汇率风险是指一个企业的成本、利润、现金流或市场价值因外汇汇率波动而潜在地上涨或下跌的风险。A项属于信用风险，不当选；B项属于利率风险，不当选；D项属于操作风险，不当选。故选C项。

items.stem: 假设一家银行今年的税后收入是 200 万元，资产总额是 10 000 万元，所有者权益为 3 000 万元，则该银行的资产收益率（ROA）是（）。
items.explanation: 资产收益率是用来衡量每单位资产创造多少净利润的指标。其计算公式：资产收益率=$净利润\div平均资产总额\times 100\%$. 因此，该银行的资产收益率$200\div10000\times 100\%=2\%$. 故选A项。

items.explanation: 丁伯根法则是由丁伯根（荷兰经济学家，首届诺贝尔经济学奖得主）提出的关于国家经济调节政策和经济调节目标之间关系的法则，其内容为：政策工具的数量或控制变量数至少要等于目标变量的数量，而且这些政策工具必须是相互独立（线性无关）的。故选 C 项。

items.stem: 一家英国公司以 “1 英镑 = 1.5 美元” 的汇率获得一笔美元贷款在国内使用，年利率为 10%。贷款到期时，汇率变成了 “1 英镑 = 1.4 美元”，如果该公司没有进行任何套期保值安排，则其实际承担的贷款利率与合同利率相比（）。
items.explanation: 由于英国采用间接标价法，因此汇率变成1英镑=1.4美元，说明英镑贬值、美元升值。到期需要用更多的英镑来偿还美元贷款，该公司实际承担的贷款利率与合同利率相比变高了。故选A项。

国际货币基金组织和世界银行是二战后成立的重要国际经济组织，根据惯例，其
总裁（行长）的人选是（）。

options.B: 国际货币基金组织由欧洲人担任，世界银行由美国人担任
options.C: 国际货币基金组织由美国人担任，世界银行由中国人担任

items.explanation: 《牙买加协定》的主要内容：取消平价和中心汇率，允许会员国自由选择汇率制度；废除黄金官价，各国中央银行可按市价自由进行交易；减少黄金的货币作用，使特别提款权成为主要国际储备资产，加强基金组织对国际清偿能力的监督；扩大对发展中国家的资金融通，设立信托基金，以优惠条件向最贫穷的发展中国家提供贷款，扩大基金组织信贷部分的贷款额度。故选 B 项。

items.explanation: 本题案例属于不足额投保情形，《中华人民共和国保险法》第五十五条规定：“保险金额低于保险价值的，除合同另有约定外，保险人按照保险金额与保险价值的比例承担赔偿责任。”即本题中保险公司应赔偿金额$=20\times (30\div60)=10$（万元）。故选D项。

items.explanation: 射幸合同是指合同的效果在订约时不能确定的合同，即合同当事人一方不必然履行给付义务，而只有当合同中约定的条件具备或合同约定的事件发生时才履行。故选B项。

items.stem: 薛芳以丈夫赵强为被保险人向保险公司投保了一份 10 年期两全保险，指定儿子赵照为受益人，在保险期间内赵强因病去世，享有保险金请求权的是（）。
items.explanation: 两全保险是指被保险人在保险合同约定的保险期间内死亡，或在保险期间届满仍生存时，保险人按照保险合同约定均应承担给付保险金责任的人寿保险。在两全保险中，当被保险人在保险期间内死亡时，保险人按合同约定将死亡保险金支付给受益人，保险合同终止；若被保险人生存至保险期间届满，保险人将生存保险金支付给被保险人。故选 B 项。

items.stem: 关于社会保险与商业保险，以下陈述错误的是（）。

options.A: 社会保险具有立法强制性，商业保险通常为自愿参加
options.B: 社会保险具有福利性和政策性，商业保险以营利性为目标
options.C: 社会保险比商业保险覆盖人群更广、保障水平更高
options.D: 商业保险可以接受政府委托，办理某些项目的社会保险

items.explanation: 随着我国经济发展和人民生活水平的不断提高，商业保险对“广覆盖，低水平”的社会保险的补充作用在我国的保障系统中变得越来越重要。故选 C 项。

items.stem: 关于相互保险公司与股份保险公司的区别，以下陈述错误的是（）。

options.A: 相互保险公司没有资本金
options.B: 相互保险公司没有股东
options.C: 相互保险公司不以追逐利润为经营目的
options.D: 相互保险公司筹资更为便利

items.explanation: 相互保险公司是由所有被保险人自行设立的保险公司组织，其目的是为所有投保人提供低成本的保险产品，而不是追求利润。相互保险公司没有股东，没有资本，不能发行股票。相互保险公司成立初期所需的资金一般是通过借款和外部融资筹集的，成员也以其保费为基础，参与公司的收益分配，弥补公司亏损。故选D项。

items.stem: 关于商业银行与保险公司的资产负债管理，以下陈述错误的是（）。

options.A: 二者都非常重视流动性管理
options.B: 通常商业银行的资产期限比负债期限长，人寿保险公司则反之
options.C: 商业银行的资产种类比保险公司更多样
options.D: 商业银行的信用风险所占的资本权重大于保险公司的信用风险所占的资本权重

items.explanation: 保险公司和商业银行都非常注重流动性管理，A项正确，不当选；商业银行容易出现借短贷长的情况，通常资产长于负债，而保险公司的负债期限很长，特别是寿险公司，负债长达20年，B项正确，不当选；商业银行的投资方向有较多的限制，而从保险公司资产来看，保险资金投资的范围和领域非常广泛，几乎涉及经济发展的各个领域，C项错误，当选；商业银行的贷款业务量较大，所以商业银行的信用风险所占的资本权重大于保险公司的信用风险所占的资本权重，D项正确，不当选。故选C项。

items.stem: 下列关于边际技术替代率的说法，正确的有（）。

options.A: 等产量曲线上某一点的边际技术替代率就是等产量曲线在该点斜率的绝对值
options.B: 边际技术替代率还可以表示为两种生产要素的边际产量之比

items.explanation: 等产量曲线上某一点的边际技术替代率就是等产量曲线在该点斜率的绝对值，A项正确，当选；边际技术替代率是指在产量保持不变的前提条件下，增加一种生产要素的数量与可以减少的另一种生产要素的数量之比。边际技术替代率等于两种生产要素的边际产量之比，B项正确，当选。通常，由于生产过程中投入的生产要素是不完全替代的，随着一种生产要素数量的增加，该要素对另外一种要素的边际技术替代率是递减的，C项正确，当选。故选ABC项。

items.stem: 在一个存在金融监管差异的国际市场中，可能出现的现象有（）。
items.explanation:
在一个存在金融监管差异的国际市场中，有可能出现两种现象：监管竞争和监管套利（AB项当选）。金融监管的溢出效应是指任何一国针对本国金融机构所作出的监管决策将影响机构的经营行为，进而会波及该机构在国际金融机构市场上的经营行为，而各国金融机构在国际市场上的业务联系使得这种行为的调整可能会影响到该机构的合作者或对手，进而会对他国的金融机构产生影响，这体现了金融监管的国际化，D项不当选。监管协调是解决监管差异化所带来的问题的方法，C项不当选。故选AB项。
在固定汇率制度、资本自由流动的条件下，财政政策有效、货币政策无效。故选 BC 项。

items.stem: （）属于商业银行的表外业务。
items.explanation:
狭义的表外业务一般包括以下三种类型：
（1）担保类业务。担保类业务是指商业银行接受客户的委托对第三方承担责任的业务，包括担保（保函）、备用信用证、跟单信用证、承兑等。
（2）承诺业务。承诺业务是指商业银行在未来某一日期按照事先约定的条件向客户提供约定的信用业务，包括票据发行便利等。
（3）金融衍生交易类业务。金融衍生交易类业务是指商业银行为满足客户保值或自身头寸管理等需要而进行的货币和利率的远期、期权等衍生交易业务。
故选 AD 项。

items.stem:
为纠正商业银行粗放和低效率的流动性管理，《巴塞尔协议Ⅲ》首次在全球范围内引入的衡量流动性监管的量化指标包括（）。
内引入的衡量流动性监管的量化指标包括（）。
items.explanation:
《巴塞尔协议Ⅲ》提出了两个流动性量化监管指标：
（1）流动性覆盖率。用于衡量在短期压力情景下（30日内）单个银行的流动性状况。

items.stem: 加强宏观审慎监管的必要性在于（）。

options.A: 金融创新过度导致系统性风险加大
options.B: 微观审慎监管对顺周期性无能为力
options.C: 金融全球化发展促使风险在全球范围内传递
options.D: 金融市场同质性加速金融市场不稳定性

items.explanation: 加强宏观审慎监管的必要性在于防范系统性金融风险，防止金融系统对经济体系的负外部溢出。具体来说，加强宏观审慎监管的必要性包括以下几点：（1）金融创新过度导致系统性风险加大；（2）微观审慎监管对顺周期性无能为力；（3）金融全球化发展促使风险在全球范围内传递；（4）金融市场同质性加速金融市场不稳定性；（5）建立健全宏观审慎政策框架；（6）强化逆周期管理；（7）提升重点机构和领域的稳健性；（8）控制金融体系的顺周期性和跨部门风险传染。通过这些措施，宏观审慎监管有助于提高金融体系的韧性和稳健性，降低金融危机发生的可能性和破坏性，促进金融体系的整体健康与稳定。故选 ABCD 项。

items.explanation: 保险中介是指介于保险经营机构之间或保险经营机构与投保人之间，专门从事保险业务咨询与销售、风险管理与安排、价值衡量与评估、损失鉴定与理算等中介服务活动，并从中依法获取佣金或手续费的单位或个人。保险中介人的主体形式多样，主要包括保险代理人、保险经纪人和保险公估人等。此外，一些其他专业领域的单位或个人也可以从事某些特定的保险中介服务，如保险精算师事务所、事故调查机构和律师等。故选 BCD 项。

items.explanation: 《中华人民共和国保险法》第三十一条规定，投保人对下列人员具有保险利益：本人；配偶、子女、父母；前项以外与投保人有抚养、赡养或者扶养关系的家庭其他成员、近亲属；与投保人有劳动关系的劳动者。除前款规定外，被保险人同意投保人为其订立合同的，视为投保人对被保险人具有保险利益。订立合同时，投保人对被保险人不具有保险利益的，合同无效。故选 ABCD 项。

items.stem: It is indicated in the first paragraph that ___ .

options.A: the strength of high-speed trading firms is the computerization
options.B: the profits of high-speed trading are declining in recent years
options.C: all the high-speed firms are no longer profitable
options.D: every high-speed trader can make more money than the traditional traders

items.explanation: 主旨题。题目意为：第一段表明 ___ 。A 项，高速交易公司的优势在于计算机化；B 项，近年来高速交易的利润在下降；C 项，所有的高速公司都不再营利了；D 项，每一个高速交易者都能比传统交易者赚更多的钱。根据第一段中 “struggling” “down 35 percent from last year and 74 percent from the peak of two years ago” 可知，本段主要是说高速交易利润有所下降。故选 B 项。
items.passage:
High – speed trading firms—the lightning – quick, computerized companies that have risen in the last decade to dominate the nation's stock market—are now struggling to hold onto their gains. Profits from high – speed trading in American stocks are reported to be, at most, $1.25 billion this year, down 35 percent from last year and 74 percent from the peak of two years ago, according to estimates from the brokerage firm Rosenblatt Securities.
While no official data is available about the employment at the high – speed firms, interviews with more than a dozen industry participants suggest that firms large and small have been cutting staff, and in some cases have shut down. The firms also account for a declining percentage of a
shrinking pool of stock trading, from 61 percent three years ago to 51 percent now.
It is a swift reversal for trading firms that have often looked like profit machines in the eyes of other investors, thanks to high-powered software and super fast data connections that can take advantage of small changes in the price of a stock. High-speed trading is far from disappearing from the market, but the struggles facing these firms are welcomed by some traditional traders and investors who have viewed the firms as formidable rivals, or worse, market manipulators that create sudden increases and drops in share prices. Peter Costa, a long-time trader on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange, said the fading presence of the firms could “restore some order to stock markets”.
Regulators are still trying to understand whether the rise of high – speed firms has been a net benefit or loss for investors, so it is hard to say how the decline of these firms will affect the markets. Many market experts have argued that the technical problems that have recently hit the market have been a result of broader trend of the market turning into dozens of automated trading services and a lack of human oversight.

items.stem: According to the first two paragraphs, the decline of high-speed trading firms is characterized by ___ .

options.B: the shrink of stock trading market
options.C: the reduction of profits and employee numbers
options.D: no longer being active in the nation's stock market

items.explanation:
细节理解题。题目意为：根据前两段，高速交易公司衰落的特征是 ___ 。第一段主要说了高速交易的利润在下降，“Profits from high-speed trading in American stocks are reported to be, at most, $1.25 billion this year, down 35 percent from last year and 74 percent from the peak of two years ago, according to estimates from the brokerage firm Rosenblatt.”
Securities.”；第二段讲了一些公司在裁员甚至倒闭，“… interviews with more than a dozen industry participants suggest that firms large and small have been cutting staff, and in some cases have shut down.”。A 项，努力赚钱；B 项，股票交易市场的萎缩；C 项，利润和雇员人数的减少；D 项，不再活跃于全国股市。其中，A 项原文并未提及，B 项只提到了其中一种现象，比较片面，而 D 项说法过于绝对。故选 C 项。

options.A: believe the world's environment is not as bad as it is thought to be
options.B: think the world's environment is in an undesirable condition
options.C: are not worried about the state of the world's environment

items.explanation:
细节理解题。题目意为：根据作者的说法，大多数学生 ___ 。其实是在问学生对于环境的认知。A 项，相信世界环境并没有想象中那么糟糕；B 项，认为世界环境不好；C 项，不担心世界环境状况；D 项，对环境有深刻的认识。根据第一段学生对于要讨
论的话题 “世界的环境非常健康” 的态度 “If that were an examination topic, most students would tear it apart, offering a long list of complaints: from local smog to global climate change, from the felling (砍伐) of forest to the extinction of species.” 可知，学生认为目前世界环境的状态并不好。故选 B 项。
items.passage:
“The world’s environment is surprisingly healthy. Discuss.” If that were an examination topic, most students would tear it apart, offering a long list of complaints: from local smog to global climate change, from the felling (砍伐) of forest to the extinction of species. The list would largely be accurate, the concern legitimate. Yet the students who should be given the highest marks would actually be those who agreed with the statement. The surprise is how good things are, not how bad.
After all, the world’s population has more than tripled during this century, and world output has risen hugely, so you would expect the earth itself to have been affected. Indeed, if people lived, consumed and produced things in the same way as they did in 1900 (or in 1950 or in 1980), the world by now would be a pretty disgusting place: smelly, dirty, toxic and dangerous.
But they don’t. The reasons why they don’t, and why the environment has not been ruined, have to do with prices, technological innovation, social change and government regulation in response to popular pressure. That is why today’s environmental problems in the poor countries ought, in principle, to be solvable.
Raw materials have not run out, and show no sign of doing so. Logically, one day they must: the planet is a finite place. Yet it is also very big, and man is very ingenious. What has happened is that every time a material seems to be running short, the price has risen and, in response, people have looked for new sources of supply, tried to find ways to use less of the material, or looked for a new substitute. For this reason, prices for energy and for minerals have fallen in real terms.
during the century. The same is true for food. Prices fluctuate, in response to harvests, natural disasters and political instability, and when they rise, it takes some time before new sources of supply become available. But they always do, assisted by new farming and crop technology. The long-term trend has been downwards.
It is where prices and markets do not operate properly that this benign（良性的）trend begins to stumble, and the genuine problems arise. Markets cannot always keep the environment healthy. If no one owns the resource concerned, no one has an interest in conserving it or fostering it: fish is the best example of this.

items.stem: 【原文题干缺失，待补】

options.A: They were in ever – increasing demand.
options.B: They were not profitable to producers.
options.C: They were subject to taxation in many places.
options.D: They were no longer considered necessities of life.

items.explanation: 细节理解题。题目意为：亚当·斯密针对糖、酒和烟草主要说了些什么？A项，它们的需求不断增加；B项，它们没有给生产商带来利润；C项，它们在许多地方都要纳税；D项，它们不再被认为是生活必需品。第一段引用了亚当·斯密的话“…and which are, therefore, extremely popular subjects of taxation.”是为了说明糖、酒和烟草是纳税的常规项目，主要强调了这三者在纳税方面的特点。故选C项。
items.passage:
“Sugar, alcohol and tobacco,” economist Adam Smith once wrote, “are commodities which are nowhere necessaries of life, which have become objects of almost universal consumption, and which are, therefore, extremely popular subjects of taxation.” Two and a half centuries on, most countries impose some sort of tax on alcohol and tobacco. With surging obesity（肥胖）level putting increasing strain on public health systems, governments around the world have begun to consider taxing sugars as well.
Whether such taxes work is still a matter of debate. A preliminary review of Mexico's taxation found a fall in purchases of taxed drinks as well as a rise in sales of un-taxed and healthier drinks. By contrast, a Danish tax on foods high in fats was abandoned a year after its introduction, amid claims that consumers were avoiding it by crossing the border to Germany to satisfy their desire for cheaper, fattier food.
The food industry, in general, firmly opposes the such direct government action. Nonetheless, the industry is under pressure to demonstrate its products are healthy as well as tasty. Over the past 30 years, the industry has made some efforts to improve the quality of its products. For example, some drink manufacturers have reduced the amount of sugar, salt or fat in a product, or found an alternative ingredient. More recently, however, some companies have been investing in a more ambitious undertaking: learning how to adjust the fundamental make – up of the food they sell. For example, having salt on the outside, but none on the inside, reduces the salt content without changing the taste.
While reformulating recipes is one way to improve public health, it should be a part of the multi-sided approach. The key is to remember that there is not just one solution. To deal with obesity, a mixture of approaches will be needed. There is no silver bullet.
items.knownAnswerText: C：糖、酒和烟草是许多地方征税的对象。原解析说明题目询问亚当·斯密对这三种商品的看法，原英文题干缺失。
items.correctionNote: 恢复原先漏导的111题及其答案C；原英文题干无法确定，保留待补。

items.stem: Why have many countries started to consider taxing sugar? (☐)

options.A: They are under growing pressure to balance their national budgets.
options.B: They are under pressure to cope with the sugar – induced health problems.
options.C: The practice of taxing alcohol and tobacco has been very profitable.
options.D: The sugar industry is making huge profits.

items.explanation: 细节理解题。题目意为：为什么许多国家开始考虑对糖征税？A项，他们在平衡国家预算方面的压力越来越大；B项，他们在应付糖引起的健康问题方面承受着压力；C项，对烟酒征税的做法非常有利可图；D项，制糖业正在赚取巨额利润。由第一段最后一句“With surging obesity（肥胖）level putting increasing strain on public health systems, governments around the world have begun to consider taxing sugars as well.”可知，对糖征税是因为考虑到了糖和健康的关系。故选B项。
items.passage:
“Sugar, alcohol and tobacco,” economist Adam Smith once wrote, “are commodities which are nowhere necessaries of life, which have become objects of almost universal consumption, and which are, therefore, extremely popular subjects of taxation.” Two and a half centuries on, most countries impose some sort of tax on alcohol and tobacco. With surging obesity（肥胖）level putting increasing strain on public health systems, governments around the world have begun to consider taxing sugars as well.
Whether such taxes work is still a matter of debate. A preliminary review of Mexico's taxation found a fall in purchases of taxed drinks as well as a rise in sales of un-taxed and healthier drinks. By contrast, a Danish tax on foods high in fats was abandoned a year after its introduction, amid claims that consumers were avoiding it by crossing the border to Germany to satisfy their desire for cheaper, fattier food.
The food industry, in general, firmly opposes the such direct government action. Nonetheless, the industry is under pressure to demonstrate its products are healthy as well as tasty. Over the past 30 years, the industry has made some efforts to improve the quality of its products. For example, some drink manufacturers have reduced the amount of sugar, salt or fat in a product, or found an alternative ingredient. More recently, however, some companies have been investing in a more ambitious undertaking: learning how to adjust the fundamental make – up of the food they sell. For example, having salt on the outside, but none on the inside, reduces the salt content without changing the taste.
While reformulating recipes is one way to improve public health, it should be a part of the multi-sided approach. The key is to remember that there is not just one solution. To deal with obesity, a mixture of approaches will be needed. There is no silver bullet.

options.A: There is no hope of success without public cooperation.
options.B: There is no single easy quick solution to the obesity problem.
options.C: There is no hurry in solving the obesity problem.

items.explanation: 语义理解题。题目意为：作者说“没有什么好办法”是什么意思？A项，没有公共合作就没有成功的希望；B项，肥胖问题没有一个简单快速的解决办法；C项，解决肥胖问题并不着急；D项，没有有效的方法来减少糖的消耗。由文章最后一段中“The key is to remember that there is not just one solution. items.stem: What is said about the financial – literacy education in the second paragraph? ( )

options.A: Many local schools add financial courses to their curriculum.
options.B: The supporters of such education become doubtful.
options.C: Financial know-how in class is definitely helpful in real life.
options.D: Financial-literacy movement helped students make wise financial decisions.

items.explanation: 细节理解题。题目意为：第二段中对金融知识教育有何看法？A项，许多地方学校在课程中增加了金融课程；B项，这种教育的支持者开始怀疑；C项，课堂上的金融知识对现实生活绝对有帮助；D项，金融知识运动帮助学生作出明智的金融决策。由第二段“School districts in many states are adding money – management courses to their curriculum. The government is encouraging students to compete in the National Financial Capability Challenge.”可知，该教育已经在美国很多州的课程中施行。故选A项。
items.passage:
Of all the lessons taught by the financial crisis, the most personal has been that we Americans should not be proud of our financial skills. We take out home loans we can't afford. We run up sky – high credit – card debts. We don't save nearly enough for retirement.
In response, supporters of financial – literacy education are raising their voices. School
districts in many states are adding money – management courses to their curriculum. The government is encouraging students to compete in the National Financial Capability Challenge. However, there is little evidence that traditional efforts to boost financial know–how help students make better decisions outside the classroom. Even as the financial–literacy movement has gained steam over the past decade, scores have been falling on tests that measure how well students perform in making financial decisions.
Given the situation, a growing number of researchers and educators agree that a more radical approach is needed. They advocate starting financial education a lot earlier than high school, putting real money and spending decisions into kids' hands, and encouraging students to talk openly about the emotions and social influences about spending.
Yet even the skeptics are slow to write off financial education completely. “We need to rigorously study the financial decisions of alumni like Ariel and Alex and compare with those of peers who didn’t get the same sort of education. Until you have experimental evidence, it is too speculative to recommend one education approach over another,” says Mike Sheden, a professor at Washington University in St. Louis who is conducting a seven-year study on whether giving children real bank accounts would result in long-term smart financial decisions. Yes, good, solid research like this takes a lot of time and resources, but it is in our own best interest to pursue it.

options.C: Putting kids in financial environment to learn from real – life experiences.

items.explanation: 语义理解题。题目意为: 第三段中提到的 “radical approach” 指的是什么? A 项, 减少金融课程的课堂教学; B 项, 从高中开始而不是从大学开始金融教育; C 项, 让孩子们在金融环境中学习现实生活中的经验; D 项, 避免讨论消费的情感和社会影响。第三段中心句 “They advocate starting financial education a lot earlier than high school, putting real money and spending decisions into kids' hands, and encouraging students to talk openly about the emotions and social influences about spending.”, 是对 “radical approach” 的解释, 即把真正的钱和支出决定交给孩子们, 公开谈论与我们的支出方式相关的情感和社会影响, 对应 C 项。故选 C 项。

items.stem: What does Mike Sheden think of the financial education of Ariel and Alex? ( )

options.C: It turns out to be a failure.
options.D: It needs experimental evidence to prove its success.

items.explanation:
细节理解题。题目意为：Mike Sheden 对 Ariel 和 Alex 的金融教育有何看法？A 项，毫无疑问，这是卓有成效的；B 项，这比他们的同龄人好；C 项，结果是失败了；D 项，它需要实验证据来证明它的成功。根据 Mike Sheden 所说 “We need to rigorously study the financial decisions of alumni like Ariel and Alex and compare with those of peers who didn't get the same sort of education. 认为应该对其教育方法进行验证。故选D项。
